summary: This document (L4) is a research discussion card arguing that a favorable DunedinPACE or GrimAge blood DNA methylation clock shift alone is insufficient as a primary healthspan endpoint. It proposes a multi-domain concordance rule requiring co-movement of ≥2 of {VO₂, muscle function, brain organ-age, immune organ-age} alongside the clock shift. The document is a conceptual/analytical critique grounded in published literature, not a primary experimental study.

content_blocks.title: Core Claim and Framing
content_blocks.content: The document asserts that a favorable blood DNAm DunedinPACE or GrimAge shift alone is NOT a sufficient primary healthspan endpoint. The proposed standard requires co-movement of ≥2 of {VO₂, muscle function, brain organ-age, immune organ-age} in the same subjects alongside the clock shift — termed a 'pre-registered multi-domain concordance rule.' The baseline being challenged is the common longevity trial and consumer framing that treats a slowed DunedinPACE or GrimAge tick as healthspan certification.

content_blocks.title: Mechanism Sketch — Construct Mismatch
content_blocks.content: DunedinPACE and GrimAge are blood methylation pace/composite surrogates. Oh-class organ ages are plasma proteomic organ-of-origin models — fundamentally different constructs. Key distinctions: (1) GrimAge is a blood DNAm lifespan/healthspan composite (PMID 30669119, Lu); (2) CALERIE trial shows within-blood discordance — DunedinPACE slows but GrimAge/PhenoAge do not change significantly (PMID 37118425, Waziry); (3) Blood vs. muscle DNAm age accelerations associate only weakly (PMID 34001218, Sillanpää). Authors of the CALERIE DNAm analysis defer conclusive geroscience proof to disease/mortality endpoints.

content_blocks.title: Actionable Limitations Identified
content_blocks.content: Three core limitations are identified: (1) Construct mismatch — blood DNAm clocks ≠ proteomic organ ages; not interchangeable endpoints. (2) Within-blood clock discordance — CALERIE already falsifies unitary 'the clock moved' framing. (3) Tissue/function gap — blood clock ≠ muscle aging; VO₂/muscle not proven redundant with clock Δ.

content_blocks.title: Prior Art / Supporting Literature
content_blocks.content: Four key references cited: (1) PMID 38057571 / DOI 10.1038/s41586-023-06802-1 — Oh 2023 Nature 624:164–172: plasma proteomic organ ages; organ-specific disease/mortality risk. (2) PMID 40634782 / DOI 10.1038/s41591-025-03798-1 — Oh 2025 Nat Med: UKB-scale organ ages; aged brain raises AD risk ~APOE4-comparable. (3) PMID 37118425 / PMC10148951 — Waziry: CALERIE CR slows DunedinPACE; GrimAge/PhenoAge NS; authors require hard healthy-aging endpoints for conclusive test. (4) PMID 35029144 / PMC8853656 — Belsky: DunedinPACE blood DNAm pace biomarker.

content_blocks.title: Refutation Criteria and Research Gap
content_blocks.content: The claim would be refuted if: In a pre-registered cohort/trial with DNAm + VO₂/muscle and/or brain+immune organ-age, a favorable DunedinPACE or GrimAge Δ alone predicts hard healthspan benefit (disease/mortality or pre-registered multi-domain composite) with effect size ≥ the co-domain package, and co-domains are redundant (clock alone matches multi-domain concordance). Key research gap: PubMed search for DunedinPACE/GrimAge ∩ organ-age co-panel studies = 0 hits — this co-measurement has not been done.

key_findings: Blood DNAm clocks (DunedinPACE, GrimAge) and plasma proteomic organ ages (Oh-class) are fundamentally different constructs and are not interchangeable as healthspan endpoints.

CALERIE trial demonstrates within-blood clock discordance: caloric restriction slows DunedinPACE but does NOT significantly change GrimAge or PhenoAge (PMID 37118425), undermining unitary 'clock moved' claims.
Blood vs. skeletal muscle DNAm age accelerations are only weakly associated (PMID 34001218, Sillanpää), indicating a tissue gap that blood clocks cannot bridge.
Plasma proteomic organ ages (Oh 2023, 2025) carry organ-specific disease and mortality signal — aged brain raises AD risk ~APOE4-comparable — not captured by blood DNAm clocks.
PubMed search for same-subject DunedinPACE/GrimAge ∩ proteomic organ-age co-panel studies under geroprotection = 0 hits — this critical co-measurement has never been performed.

Proposed multi-domain concordance rule: clock shift alone fails as healthspan certification unless ≥2 of {VO₂, muscle function, brain organ-age, immune organ-age} also move concordantly in the same subjects.
CALERIE authors themselves defer conclusive geroscience proof to disease/mortality endpoints, treating clock pharmacodynamics as supportive rather than certifying.
Estimated time to refute this assumption: 4 weeks (kill_cost_tier=1), suggesting this is a tractable but currently unaddressed research gap.
